'''Jacob Palis Jr.''' (15 March 1940 – 7 May 2025) was a Brazilian mathematician and academic. Palis's research interests were mainly [[dynamical systems]] and [[differential equations]]. Some themes are [[global stability]] and [[hyperbolicity]], [[Bifurcation theory|bifurcations]], [[attractor]]s and [[chaotic system]]s. He proposed the [[Palis' conjectures]] (which form the [[Palis' program]]),<ref>[[Carlos Matheus]], "PALIS’ CONJECTURES: A QUEST FOR A GLOBAL QUALITATIVE VIEW OF MOST DYNAMICAL SYSTEMS", ''to Jacob Palis on the occasion of his 80th anniversary'' http://carlos.matheus.perso.math.cnrs.fr/ems-palis.pdf</ref> which influenced the development of the theory of dynamical systems, and also of its applications to other sciences.<ref>{{Cite web | title=In Memoriam {{!}} ICTP | url=https://www.ictp.it/news/2025/5/memoriam | access-date=2025-08-05 | website=www.ictp.it}}</ref> He was a world leader in [[chaos theory]] research.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Jacob Palis, spécialiste de la théorie du chaos, a été moteur dans l'émergence de l'école mathématique brésilienne | url=https://www.lemonde.fr/sciences/article/2025/05/21/jacob-palis-specialiste-de-la-theorie-du-chaos-a-ete-moteur-dans-l-emergence-de-l-ecole-mathematique-bresilienne_6607611_1650684.html | access-date=2025-08-05 | website=www.lemonde.fr | date=21 May 2025 }}</ref> Palis was an influential figure in the development of mathematics in Brazil.<ref>{{Cite web | title=Nada como a incerteza - revista piauí | url=https://piaui.folha.uol.com.br/materia/nada-como-a-incerteza/ | access-date=2025-08-05 | website=piaui.folha.uol.com.br | date=29 July 2014 }}</ref>

==Life and career==
Jacob Palis was born in [[Uberaba, Minas Gerais]]. His father was a [[Lebanese Brazilians|Lebanese]] immigrant, and his mother was of [[Syrian Brazilians|Syrian]] ancestry.<ref>{{Cite web |date=2020-05-15 |title=Jacob Palis is honored in the 'Scientists of Brazil' series. |url=https://impa.br/notices/jacob-palis-is-honored-in-the-scientists-of-brazil-series/?lang=en |access-date=2026-06-22 |website=IMPA - Institute for Pure and Applied Mathematics |language=pt-BR}}</ref> The couple had eight children (five men and three women), and Jacob was the youngest. His father was a merchant, owner of a large store, and supported and funded the studies of his children. Palis said that he already enjoyed mathematics in his childhood.<ref>{{Cite web | url=http://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/wp-content/uploads/2009/07/entrevista_161.pdf | title=Revista Pesquisa Fapesp | access-date=16 April 2015 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140514114154/http://revistapesquisa.fapesp.br/wp-content/uploads/2009/07/entrevista_161.pdf | archive-date=14 May 2014 | url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="fap">[http://www.faperj.br/downloads/revista/Rio_Pesquisa_4_2008.pdf Rio Pesquisa] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924010506/http://www.faperj.br/downloads/revista/Rio_Pesquisa_4_2008.pdf |date=24 September 2015 }} </ref>

At 16, Palis moved to Rio de Janeiro to study engineering at the [[University of Brazil]] – now [[UFRJ]]. He was approved in first place in the entrance exam, but was not old enough to enroll; he then had to take the university's entry exam again a year later, where he once again finished in first place. He graduated in 1962 with honours and received the award for the best student.<ref name="fap" />

In 1964, he moved to the United States. In 1966, he obtained his master's degree in mathematics under the guidance of [[Stephen Smale]] at the [[University of California, Berkeley]], and in 1968 his PhD, with the thesis ''On Morse-Smale [[Diffeomorphism]]s'', again with Smale as advisor.<ref name="rbhm">{{Cite web| url=http://www.rbhm.org.br/issues/RBHM%20-%20vol.6%2C%20no12%2C%20outubro%20%282006%29/Cl%C3%B3vis%20-%20parte%202%20-%20RBHM%2C%20Vol.%206%2C%20no%2012%2C%20p.%20165-196%2C%202006.pdf | title=Sobre o início e consolidação da pesquisa matemática no Brasil – Parte II | language=pt | trans-title=On the beginning and consolidation of mathematical research in Brazil – Part II | access-date=7 February 2022 | archive-date=18 September 2020 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200918124321/http://www.rbhm.org.br/issues/RBHM%20-%20vol.6,%20no12,%20outubro%20(2006)/Cl%C3%B3vis%20-%20parte%202%20-%20RBHM,%20Vol.%206,%20no%2012,%20p.%20165-196,%202006.pdf | url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web | title=Jacob Palis Presidente da Academia Brasileira de Ciências| url=https://www.abc.org.br/IMG/pdf/doc-4325.pdf | access-date=7 April 2024|website=abc.org.br|page=1}}</ref>

In 1968, he returned to Brazil and became a researcher at the [[Instituto Nacional de Matemática Pura e Aplicada]] (IMPA) in [[Rio de Janeiro]], Brazil.<ref name="rbhm" />
Beginning in 1973 he held a permanent position as professor at IMPA, where he was director from 1993 until 2003. He was Secretary-General of the [[Third World Academy of Sciences]] from 2004 to 2006, and elected its president in 2006<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.ictp.trieste.it/~twas/publ/2006-09-04_Palis.html |title=Palis Elected TWAS President |access-date=4 November 2006 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20070715160922/http://www.ictp.trieste.it/~twas/publ/2006-09-04_Palis.html |archive-date=15 July 2007 }}</ref> and remained on position till December 2012. He was also president of the [[International Mathematical Union]] from 1999 to 2002.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.mathunion.org/organization/ec/ec-1952-2014/ |title=International Mathematical Union (IMU): EC 1952-2014 |access-date=3 June 2015 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108154651/http://www.mathunion.org/organization/ec/ec-1952-2014 |archive-date=8 January 2015 |url-status=dead }}</ref> He was president of the [[Brazilian Academy of Sciences]] from 2007 to 2016.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.jornaldaciencia.org.br/Detalhe.jsp?id=45834 |title=Jornal da Ciência |access-date=22 August 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://archive.today/20121129155550/http://www.jornaldaciencia.org.br/Detalhe.jsp?id=45834 |archive-date=29 November 2012 }}</ref> Palis advised more than forty [[PhD]] students so far from more than ten countries, including [[Artur Oscar Lopes]], [[Ricardo Mañé]], [[Welington de Melo]], [[Carlos Gustavo Moreira]], [[Enrique Pujals]] and [[Marcelo Viana]].<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.mathgenealogy.org/id.php?id=32570 | title=Jacob Palis, Jr. - the Mathematics Genealogy Project }}</ref>

Palis died at a hospital in [[Rio de Janeiro]], on 7 May 2025, at the age of 85. He had been hospitalized since March.<ref>[https://oglobo.globo.com/brasil/noticia/2025/05/07/morre-aos-85-anos-no-rio-o-matematico-jacob-palis.ghtml Morre aos 85 anos no Rio o matemático Jacob Palis] {{in lang|pt-br}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Palis received numerous medals and decorations. He was a foreign member of several academies of sciences, including the [[United States National Academy of Sciences]], the [[French Academy of Sciences]] and [[German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina]].<ref>{{cite web |title= Jacob Palis |url=https://www.leopoldina.org/mitgliederverzeichnis/mitglieder/member/Member/show/jacob-palis/|publisher=German Academy of Sciences Leopoldina |access-date=26 May 2021}}</ref> In 2005 Palis received the [[Legion of Honor]].

He was a member of the [[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40116 |title=Gruppe 1: Matematiske fag |publisher=[[Norwegian Academy of Science and Letters]] |language=Norwegian |access-date=7 October 2010 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131110152102/http://www.dnva.no/c26849/artikkel/vis.html?tid=40116 |archive-date=10 November 2013}}</ref> In 2010, he was awarded the [[Balzan Prize]] for his fundamental contributions in the mathematical theory of dynamical systems that has been the basis for many applications in various scientific disciplines, such as in the study of oscillations.<ref>[http://www.balzan.org/news-it/i-vincitori-dei-premi-balzan-2010_5154.html  Balzan Prize winners in 2010] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110719235930/http://www.balzan.org/news-it/i-vincitori-dei-premi-balzan-2010_5154.html |date=19 July 2011 }}, from the website of the ''Fondazione internazionale Premio Balzan''</ref><ref>[https://www.ams.org/notices/201101/rtx110100066p.pdf Notices of the AMS, Volume 58, Number 1, pages 66 and 67]</ref> He was also a recipient of the 1988 [[TWAS Prize]].<ref name="Prizes and Awards">{{Cite web |url=http://twas.org/opportunities/prizes-and-awards |title=Prizes and Awards |date=2016 |publisher=The World Academy of Sciences}}</ref>

==Selected publications==
* ''On Morse-Smale Dynamical Systems'', Topology 19, 1969 (385–405). {{doi|10.1016/0040-9383(69)90024-X}}
* ''Structural Stability Theorems'', with [[Stephen Smale|S. Smale]], Proceedings of the Institute on Global Analysis, American Math. Society, Vol. XIV, 1970 (223–232).
* ''Cycles and Bifurcations Theory'', with S. Newhouse, Asterisque 31, Société Mathématique de France, 1976 (44–140).
* ''[http://www.numdam.org/item/PMIHES_1978__48__5_0 The Topology of Holomorphic Flows near a Singularity]'', with C. Camacho and [[Nicolaas Kuiper|N. Kuiper]], Publications Math.Institut Hautes Études Scientifiques 48, 1978 (5–38).
* ''Moduli of Stability and Bifurcation Theory'', Proceedings of the International Congress of Mathematicians, Helsinki, 1978 (835–839).
* ''Stability of Parameterized Families of Gradient Vector Fields'', with [[Floris Takens|F. Takens]], Annals of Mathematics 118, 1983 (383–421). {{doi|10.2307/2006976}}
* ''Cycles and Measure of Bifurcation Sets for Two-Dimensional Diffeomorphisms'', with F. Takens, Inventiones Mathematicae 82, 1985 (397–422).  {{doi|10.1007/BF01388862}}
* ''Homoclinic Orbits, Hyperbolic Dynamic and Fractional Dimensions of Cantor Sets'' (Lefschetz Centennial Conference) Contemporary Mathematics - American Mathematical Society, 58, 1987 (203–216).
* ''Hyperbolicity and Creation of Homoclinic Orbits'', with F.Takens, Annals of Mathematics 125, 1987 (337–374). {{doi|10.2307/1971313}}
* ''On the C1 Omega-Stability Conjecture, Publications Math''. Institut Hautes Études Scientifiques, 66, 1988 (210–215).
* ''Bifurcations and Global Stability of Two-Parameter Families of Gradient Vector Fields'' with M. J. Carneiro, Publications Math. Institut Hautes Études Scientifiques 70, 1990 (103–168).
* "Homoclinic Tangencies for Hyperbolic Sets of Large Hausdorff Dimension", with [[Jean-Christophe Yoccoz|J. C. Yoccoz]], ''Acta Mathematica'' '''172''', 1994, pp.&nbsp;91–136.
* ''High Dimension Diffeomorphisms Displaying Infinitely Many Sinks'', with [[Marcelo Viana|M. Viana]], Annals of Mathematics 140, 1994 (207–250). {{doi|10.2307/2118546}}
* ''A Global View of Dynamics and a [[Palis conjecture|Conjecture on the Denseness of Finitude of Attractors]]''.  ''Astérisque''. France:, v. 261, pp.&nbsp;339–351, 2000.
* ''Homoclinic tangencies and fractal invariants in arbitrary dimension'', with [[Carlos Gustavo Moreira|C. Moreira]] and M. Viana, C R Ac Sc Paris., 2001.  {{doi|10.1016/S0764-4442(01)02085-7}}
* ''Nonuniformily hyperbolic horseshoes unleashed by homoclinic bifurcations and zero density of attractors'', with J.-C. Yoccoz, C R Ac Sc Paris., 2001.{{doi|10.1016/S0764-4442(01)02139-5}}
;Books published
* ''Geometric Theory of Dynamical Systems'', with W. de Melo. Springer-Verlag, 1982; also published in Portuguese, Russian and Chinese.
* ''Hyperbolicity and Sensitive-Chaotic Dynamics at Homoclinic Bifurcations, Fractal Dimensions and Infinitely Many Attractors'', with F. Takens. Cambridge Univ. Press, 1993; Second Edition, 1994.
